text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Guntis Ulmanis, on an official visit to the UK, visited the British Ministry of Defence and the Latvian embassy in London.

- The prime minister says he will accept the resignation of the state minister of local governments, Ernests Jurkans, a member of the Democratic Party Saimnieks. He said that he wants the post to be kept in the cabinet.
- The Riga District Court did not approve the report submitted by David Berrey, the liquidator of the Bank Baltija.
- The District Court of Valka has convicted two customs officers on bribery charges.
- The Board of the Union of Latvian Scientists called on the prime minister to sack State Minister of Higher Education Peteris Cimdins.

- State Secretary of the Latvian MFA announced that talks concerning the border with Russia will continue in either late November or early December. The Cooperation Council decided the factions are to elaborate their stance on the future of the District of Abrene.
- The Children's Hospital of Gailezers in Riga is left in the cold as it owes 113,000 lats for past heating bills.
